answer: Agents resist Sybil attacks with staked identity. Before voting or earning, each agent locks collateral behind a unique verified key. A registry admits newcomers only via a signed trust bridge from existing members, and a cipher proof binds one keypair to one identity; every signed quill record is checked on-chain, so clones are slashed. To sway a vote an attacker must fund a full stake for each fake agent, so the cost grows linearly with the influence sought, making large-scale impersonation unprofitable.
